article.headline: Insmed Soars 20.6% As Sanofi Buyout Report Hits The Tape
article.deck: The jump carried Insmed through a 137.80 buy point in a 15-week cup, and the 144.46 close sits just inside a buy range that ends at 144.69.
body: Insmed rose 24.66, or 20.6%, to 144.46 Thursday, a breakout on a day the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq each fell 2% or more. The stock cleared a 137.80 buy point in a 15-week cup, 32.7% deep, that ran from an Aug. 6 high to an Oct. 23 low. The close is 4.8% above the buy point and inside the buy range, which tops out at 144.69. Volume ran 4.67x the 50-day average.

The cup formed after a bigger correction: Insmed is still 32.1% below its 52-week high of 212.75, set Dec. 2, 2025, and that longer slide bottomed at 90.39 on June 10. The stock finished 30.3% above its 50-day line and 17.8% above its 200-day. It closed 24.4% above its 21-day exponential average, with the session's low 0.29 ATRs from the 21-day line, so the move is not stretched on that measure. RS rank is 96 of 99 on the desk's list, though the RS line is still 35.1% below its own high. Shares are up 53.6% in a month and down 17.0% year to date.

Insmed is still losing money. It lost 0.46 a share in the September quarter on revenue of $524.4 million, up 268.4% from a year earlier. Revenue has climbed every quarter in the table, from $263.8 million in the December 2025 quarter to $306.0 million, $425.5 million and $524.4 million; per-share losses ran 1.54, 0.76, 0.06 and 0.46. The market values the company at $31.69 billion, 225.06 times forward earnings.

The move came on takeover talk. Investor's Business Daily ran the headline "Sanofi Reportedly Gears Up For The Biggest Biotech Deal In Years," and Barron's headlined that Insmed stock is a winner with or without a Sanofi buyout, analysts say. Shares added 0.6% after hours to 145.27 as of 6:15 p.m. Eastern.
A close back under 137.80 would turn this into a stalled breakout.
article.watch: Whether Insmed holds the 137.80 buy point; a close above 144.69 puts it past the buy range.

fundamentals.name: AST SpaceMobile, Inc.
fundamentals.summary: AST SpaceMobile, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, designs and develops the constellation of BlueBird satellites in the United States. The company provides a cellular broadband network in space to be accessible directly by smartphones for commercial use and other applications, as well as for government use. Its SpaceMobile service provides cellular broadband services to end-users who are out of terrestrial cellular coverage. The company was founded in 2017 and is headquartered in Midland, Texas.

article.deck: Visa is 4.3% above the 385.67 buy point of a six-week flat base and inside the buy range to 404.95, with the 50-day line at 394.01 just below.
body: Visa runs the network in the middle of a card payment. VisaNet authorizes, clears and settles transactions, and the company sells credit, debit and prepaid card products along with tap to pay, tokenization and click to pay services. Visa Direct moves money across the network, letting clients collect, hold, convert and send funds.

The growth is steady rather than explosive. Revenue rose in each of the four quarters in the table, from $10.90 billion in the December 2025 quarter to $11.23 billion, $11.63 billion and $12.14 billion in the September quarter, which was up 13.2% from a year earlier. Earnings in that quarter came to 3.19 a share, up 21.8%. Per-share earnings across the four quarters ran 3.03, 3.14, 2.97 and 3.19.

The market values Visa at $750.52 billion. The stock trades at 23.47 times forward earnings and 32.65 times trailing. Shares are up 14.7% year to date and 25.2% over the past year, and RS rank is 81 of 99 on the desk's list.

Visa fell 12.97, or 3.1%, to 402.25 Thursday on volume 1.26x its 50-day average, as the major indexes each dropped 2% or more. It broke out Oct. 12 from a six-week flat base, 7.5% deep, with a 385.67 buy point; volume that day was 0.8x average. Twenty-eight sessions later it closed 4.3% above the buy point, inside the buy range that ends at 404.95. The stock finished 2.8% below its 21-day exponential average at 413.84, 0.04 ATRs under the 21-day line, and 2.1% above its 50-day line at 394.01. It is 9.0% below its 52-week high of 442.23, and the RS line is 2.5% off its high.

The day's news was a security story. Yahoo Finance reported that JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard disclosed a cyberattack on third-party vendors, and Decrypt's headline said hackers leaked Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan customer data. Separately, an Insider Monkey headline noted that Morgan Stanley raised its Visa target. After hours the stock eased 0.2% to 401.50 as of 6:05 p.m. Eastern.
The next earnings report is due Jan. 26, 2027. A close under the 50-day line at 394.01 would be the first crack in the chart since the October breakout; a hold there keeps it intact.
article.watch: The 50-day line at 394.01, which Visa now sits 2.1% above.

chief.verdict: This is a market in correction, and the leaders show it: the S&P 500 fell 2.0% to 7175.83 and the Nasdaq fell 2.3% to 23879.2, 8.8% below its 50-day line and 13.9% off its high, while AMD, RS 99, broke its 50-day line on 2.56 times normal volume. The setups that still work are slow money, not tech: GWW holding a 15-week flat base, DIS one day out of a 62-week cup with its RS line at a new high. The one big breakout, INSM up 20.6%, came on a takeover rumor, not on the base. The risk leans down until the indexes stop making new lows.
chief.market: With the S&P 500 at 8 distribution days (weighted 7.2), the Nasdaq at 7 (weighted 8.2) and both below their 50-day and 200-day lines, stay in cash and buy nothing new until a follow-through day.

picks.why: This is the best chart on the desk: a 15-week flat base only 12.9% deep, a breakout on 2026-11-04 on 2.39 times normal volume, RS 92 and EPS up 102.9%. It closed at 1423.88, 0.3% over the 1420.01 buy point, and fell only 1.7% on a day the Dow dropped 2.2%. That is how a leader acts in a correction, but this market is no place to start buying.
picks.entry: 1420.01 to 1491.01, only after a market follow-through day, and only if GWW is still holding above 1420.01 and its 21-day line at 1425.88. Two closes under 1420.01 and it goes back to watch.

picks.why: A 62-week cup, 23.0% deep, with the RS line at a new high is a sound base. It broke out on 2026-11-18 on 2.02 times volume, but gave back 1.7% today on 1.67 times volume to close at 120.25, just 0.3% over the 119.88 buy point. Heavy selling the day after a breakout is a warning, so it has to prove the breakout holds.

The 20.6% jump on 4.67 times volume came on a Sanofi takeover rumor. It closed at 144.46, right at the 144.69 top of the buy range and 30.3% above its 50-day line, out of a cup 32.7% deep, with the company still losing money; a deal headline, not the base, is setting the price.

It broke out on 2026-10-12 on 0.8 times normal volume, below average, so there was never real buying behind it. Today it fell 3.1% on 1.26 times volume to 402.25, near the top of the buy range at 404.95.
RS 98 cannot fix this chart: it is 34.5% under its 50-day line and 47.5% under the 595.61 buy point, and earnings come on 2026-11-24, five sessions out.
